message:
fix(sparsemax): subtract the row max before the cumulative sum (#1545)

## Summary

`_sparsemax_forward_kernel` computes the cumulative sum and the
threshold `(cssv - 1) / r` on the raw sorted values. Sparsemax is
shift-invariant, but in fp32 a large common offset in a row absorbs part
of the `- 1`, so the threshold and the outputs lose accuracy, and for
large-magnitude bf16/fp16 rows the result leaves the simplex. For
example, a bf16 row of 16 values equal to 9.437e7 returns 9.437e7 for
every entry instead of 1/16, and an fp16 row of 256 values equal to
-65504 returns 2/256 per entry (row sum 2).

This PR shifts each row by its maximum (the first element of the already
sorted row) before the cumulative sum and before the final `x - tau`, as
reference sparsemax implementations do. Rows whose maximum is not finite
(all `-inf`, a `+inf` or a NaN entry) are shifted by 0, so their output
is unchanged from `main`. The backward kernel is unchanged.

How much this matters for realistic inputs: on standard-normal rows with
a common offset, the error of `main` grows with the offset, but stays
moderate. Over 72 cases (fp32 and bf16; widths 256, 1024, 4096, 32768;
offsets 0, 10, 100; 3 seeds), `main`'s max error against a float64
sparsemax exceeded 100× the error of a plain PyTorch fp32 sparsemax (or
2 unit roundoffs of the largest output, whichever is larger) in one
case: fp32, width 32768, offset 100, at 101.8×. The other fp32
offset-100 cases were 51× to 90×, the fp32 offset-10 cases 4× to 17×,
and bf16 was not affected (at most 0.31×). The off-simplex results need
large-magnitude inputs such as the bf16 and fp16 rows above.

## Testing Done

Before (`main` 67d7222) vs after (this branch), same inputs in the same
process, against a float64 sparsemax:

| input | max abs error before | after | max \|row sum − 1\| before |
after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fp32 `randn(8, 32768) + 100` | 9.8e-06 | 4.0e-08 | 6.9e-05 | 1.8e-07 |
| fp32 `randn(8, 256) + 100` | 1.0e-05 | 2.0e-08 | 3.1e-05 | 8.9e-08 |
| bf16 `full((1, 16), 9.437e7)` | 9.4e+07 | 0 | 1.5e+09 | 0 |
| fp16 `full((1, 256), -65504)` | 3.9e-03 | 0 | 1.0 | 0 |

Error relative to a PyTorch fp32 sparsemax (same definition as above;
108 cases: fp32, bf16, fp16 × widths 256–32768 × offsets 0/10/100 × 3
seeds):

- fp32: before 1.6–101.8 (offset 0: 1.6–3.4; offset 10: 4.1–17.0; offset
100: 51.2–101.8); after 0.00–0.47 in every case.
- bf16 and fp16: identical before and after (0.08–0.31). In 3 bf16 cases
at offset 100 the row-sum error after the fix is 3.42e-03 instead of
1.95e-03 (bf16 output rounding; the max error against float64 is
unchanged), and in one fp16 case 2.25e-04 instead of 2.21e-04. No case
has a larger max error after the fix.
- Non-finite rows (some `-inf`, all `-inf`, one `+inf`, one NaN, all
zeros): output identical to `main`, NaN positions included.
- Backward on fp32 `randn(4, 1024) + 100`: max |dx − dx_float64| 4.8e-08
before and after.
- Forward time, median of 50 (ms), before → after: fp32 (4096, 1024)
0.334 → 0.338; fp32 (1024, 4096) 0.375 → 0.371; fp32 (64, 32768) 0.348 →
0.368 (+6%; +1% in an earlier run of the same change, so partly noise,
but possibly a small cost at this shape); bf16 (4096, 1024) 0.349 →
0.338; bf16 (1024, 4096) 0.374 → 0.367; bf16 (64, 32768) 0.337 → 0.343.
- `test/transformers/test_sparsemax.py`: 9 passed, 1 skipped, before and
after. The skipped test (`test_sparsemax_large_row_offset`) needs 17.2
GB of free GPU memory; this GPU has 16 GB.

- Hardware Type: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 Laptop GPU (16 GB); torch
2.11.0+cu128, triton 3.6.0
- [ ] run `make test` to ensure correctness (not run in full; only
`test/transformers/test_sparsemax.py`, see above)
- [x] run `make checkstyle` to ensure code style (via the repo's
pre-commit hooks, ruff v0.14.11 check and format: both pass on the
changed file)
- [ ] run `make test-convergence` to ensure convergence (not run)

@@ -35,6 +35,12 @@ def _sparsemax_forward_kernel(
         cache_modifier=".cg",
     ).to(tl.float32)
 
+    # sparsemax is shift-invariant: subtract the row max so that a large common offset does not
+    # absorb the "- 1" in the threshold (rows whose max is not finite are left unshifted)
+    z_max = tl.load(ptr_sorted_x_data_row).to(tl.float32)
+    z_max = tl.where(tl.abs(z_max) < float("inf"), z_max, 0.0)
+    z_sorted_block = z_sorted_block - z_max
+
     z_valid = tl.where(mask, z_sorted_block, 0.0)
     cssv = tl.cumsum(z_valid, 0)
 
@@ -58,7 +64,7 @@ def _sparsemax_forward_kernel(
         cache_modifier=".cg",
     ).to(tl.float32)
 
-    y = tl.maximum(x_block - tau, 0.0)
+    y = tl.maximum((x_block - z_max) - tau, 0.0)
 
     tl.store(
         ptr_output_row + offs,
